articles.content:
Lance Broadway, a former Major League Baseball pitcher-turned-actor who appeared in Marvel’s “Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.,” has died at 43.

Broadway was found dead on Nov. 17 in an apartment complex stairwell in Dallas, Texas, according to the Dallas County Medical Examiner . His cause of death is pending autopsy results.

Broadway was a pitcher who played for the Chicago White Sox and New York Mets. He made his feature film debut in 2013’s “Olympus Has Fallen” as Secret Service Agent O’Neill under President Benjamin Asher (Aaron Eckhart). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘Bad Day’ Trailer: Cameron Diaz Is a Single Mom Who Accidentally Robs a Bank in Netflix Comedy 'KPop Demon Hunters' Golden World Tour Sets 2027 Arena Dates

His television career included appearances on “Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.,” “Lucifer,” “Saint George,” “Kevin From Work” and “Real Husbands of Hollywood.” His most recent credit was on two episodes of USA Network’s “Colony” in 2016-17.

Broadway was cast as Commander Linden in “Teleios,” which was later renamed “Beyond the Trek,” in 2014. The science fiction thriller was released as a TV movie in 2017. He was cast as Devon in the short film “Shattered Reflections” in 2015.

Born in Bryan, Texas, Broadway was an all-district baseball player in high school and went on to pitch for Dallas Baptist University. He transferred to Texas Christian University, where he was named conference pitcher of the year before being selected 15th overall by the Chicago White Sox in the 2005 Major League Baseball draft. He made his Major League debut in 2007 and was traded to the New York Mets in 2009. He signed a minor league deal with the Toronto Blue Jays that same year but never played for the team.

articles.title: 5 Game of Thrones Characters Totally Ruined by the HBO TV Series
articles.summary: There's no denying that Game of Thrones is one of the greatest shows in television history. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google There's no denying that Game of Thrones is one of the greatest shows in television history. There's also no denying that the series ultimately failed many of its major characters and storylines with its widely panned final season. Jon Snow's clearly important parentage played no part in those last few episodes, Daenerys Targaryen's turn to "mad queen" felt rushed, Jaime Lannister's arc was totally tossed aside, and the villainous Cersei Lannister got one of the most unsatisfying endings ever. That said, most of the time we spent with those characters on the show was great, intriguing, and felt true to who they were in the books.

While you could write pages about those characters, they were hurt by the fact that the books aren't finished. We're discussing the characters who were more interesting in the A Song of Ice and Fire novels, yet the adaptations brought to Game of Thrones on the small screen reduced them to one or two smaller aspects and resulted in disappointing versions. In some cases, they were good but better in the books, while in other situations, the show turned them into hollow shells of what they could have been.

Stannis Baratheon is incredibly unlikable in both the show and the novels, yet the books make sure he's a bit more nuanced. He's driven by his duty and the fact that he understands the Iron Throne to be his by birthright, rather than because he's greedy and wants it. The show has him be complicit in Melisandre's killing of his brother Renly and he often comes across as a religious zealot for the Lord of Light (though not quite as much as his wife is).

The novels use his belief in Melisandre alongside his own beliefs in his duties, which play against each other. It makes for intriguing chapters, especially through the eyes of POV character Davos. It's unclear if Stannis would actually burn his daughter alive in the books, but if he did, it would likely be better fleshed out than due to bad weather ahead of a battle. Stannis will never be anyone's favorite character, but he's a pivotal piece of the story and works well as a cautionary tale for others vying for the throne, so the show turning him into someone far less interesting is disappointing.

Varys is one of those characters who is good in the show, yet when you read about him, you gain a whole new appreciation for him. The Master of Whisperers was always a step ahead of everyone outside of maybe Littlefinger. While that is depicted well on the screen, the Varys of the books is something else entirely. For starters, we never get to see how he's a master of disguise. In the novels, Varys takes on many forms and can change the way he speaks so he's unrecognizable. Even Tyrion takes a while to realize who he's talking to at one point.

Varys is also more of a Targaryen loyalist in the books (some theories even say Varys is actually a Targaryen ) and is even rumored to be behind the plot that allows Young Griff, Rhaegar's actual son, to escape King's Landing as a baby. The Young Griff subplot is one of the biggest mysteries left in the novels. As the show went on and avoided that story, Varys became less cunning and far less interesting.

This may be a controversial pick because Robb Stark feels more prominent in the show. In the novels, he and Rickon are the only Starks who aren't POV characters, so Robb's story is seen through the eyes of Catelyn. In Game of Thrones , we watch plenty of scenes from his rise as the King in the North to his untimely death at the Red Wedding. However, the show made a major change that made Robb worse as a character.

In the books, Robb is comforted by Jeyne Westerling after learning of his brothers' supposed deaths. They sleep together and Robb marries her to protect her honor, while in the show, Robb simply falls for Talisa and throws everything away to marry her. This takes away from a key aspect of Robb's story, which is how his downfall mirrors that of Ned Stark. He's so much like his father that his honor and honesty lead him to marry Jeyne instead of the Frey he was promised to, resulting in the Red Wedding. Without that honor aspect, Robb is just someone who made a bad decision with his heart, which is far less intriguing.

A Feast for Crows is often seen as the worst book in A Song of Ice and Fire , yet it does shine a light on the Martells and the Grejoys. That means a lot of time is given to Euron Greyjoy, who is one of the scariest characters in the franchise. He's someone who is incredibly ambitious while also being increasingly dangerous. He basically wants to become a god, steal a dragon, and is willing to dabble in the dark arts to get what he wants.

Euron's standing heading into The Winds of Winter is one of the most interesting elements of the series. He could change the face of Westeros and the battle for the Iron Throne entirely. Unfortunately, Game of Thrones changed him into a generic, campy villain. The TV show counterpart doesn't seem nearly as threatening and his ambition often comes down to wanting to have sex with the Queen. Nothing captivating about Euron remained and what we got was a hollow shell of someone who could've changed the game in the final seasons.

It might be kind of a cop-out to group all of Dorne together but Game of Thrones messed them all up so badly that it's hard not to. In the books, Doran Martell is a cunning man who is playing the long game in his desire for revenge against the Lannisters, to the point where almost nobody knows what he's planning. The strategic elements of his story are some of the highlights of the last few books. The show just plays on the idea that he's weak, which he's mostly feigning in the novels, and doesn't do anything beyond that, making him a passive character.

The Sand Snakes are ruined in the show by becoming interchangable. They give no time to differentiate Oberyn's daughters, so nobody cares about them. In the books, each has their own nuanced personality, are diverse, and each is carrying out a plot from Doran , adding so much to the Dorne storylines. The show also entirely cut Doran's heir Ariane Martell, who had her own great plans, and basically melded some of those ideas into Ellaria and the Sand Snakes. What should've been a gripping political subplot was reduced to nothing of interest and viewers often groaned when a Dorne scene came on TV, which isn't how it should've been.

Which A Song of Ice and Fire character do you think Game of Thrones messed up the most? Let us know in the comments.

articles.content:
Playbill is apologizing for running an ad for singers for a cast album called "George Floyd the Musical" from the Busted Broadway company.

The project drew numerous negative comments from Broadway stars and many others. Busted Broadway responded on its social media Thursday that "The project 'George Floyd the Musical' is NOT making light of, condoning, or mocking the horrific 2020 murder of George Floyd. It’s a satire on the CULTURE, rather than the person. Never judge a show by its title, as many who have never seen the script or score appear to be doing now.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘Gordon,’ a Big Netflix Series From Argentina, Unpacked by Pablo Trapero and Star Rodrigo de la Serna 'Stranger Things' Prequel Spinoff 'Other Worlds' Ordered to Series at Netflix

Once leadership was alerted, the listing was immediately removed, and we began reviewing and revising our approval processes. We apologize unequivocally for giving this hateful listing any further air, and we promise to do better going forward. We at Playbill aim to lift up this community with empathy, consideration, and respect. We hope those who read and follow us do the same.

"We know this listing has upset and offended many, and the fact that it made it onto our site has disappointed those who trust us as an outlet," the post continued.

articles.title: Dragon Ball Super Already Locked In the Next Z Fighter & They Need Their Anime Debut
articles.summary: Almost every Dragon Ball arc adds another warrior to the Z Fighters, and Granolah looks like he could be next. The last remaining Cerealian boasts all the key characteristics that fit into Goku's band of highly moral misfits. Granolah survived the destruction of his planet thanks to Bardock, but it doesn't come without collateral damage. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Almost every Dragon Ball arc adds another warrior to the Z Fighters, and Granolah looks like he could be next. The last remaining Cerealian boasts all the key characteristics that fit into Goku's band of highly moral misfits. Granolah survived the destruction of his planet thanks to Bardock, but it doesn't come without collateral damage. The situation creates Granolah's deep disdain toward the Saiyans, by proxy of Frieza. He doesn't care where the sole blame lays at the start of his arc, but he eventually understands that the evil emperor is to blame. The manga introduced him some time ago, but he awaits his anime debut .

Granolah also didn't join up with the Z Fighters after his arc was completed. Goku and Vegeta offered him up the opportunity to come train with them. However, he decides to stay and gather the Dragon Balls. He currently continues his journey and hasn't made an appearance since in the manga. The way Granolah's story ends is incomplete, so there's no way he won't get an expanded role later .

Similar to Tien, Piccolo and Vegeta, these former foes turned allies realize what a good person Goku is and what he's trying to accomplish. Vegeta in particular looks to just avenge his planet, similar to Granolah, but goes the wrong way about it initially. His change to the Z Fighters took some more time, but Granolah ran through similar problems. He's never told about Bardock protecting him . He's just told the Saiyans caused his race's destruction.

Granolah works for the Heeters, who use his disdain for the Saiyans, to try and defeat Goku and Vegeta. The plan backfires, as Granolah discovers the truth and flips sides. Even though he's not a Saiyan or Namekian, Granolah has proven himself to be a competent fighter and representative of his race. Cerealians use an enhanced right eye to find their opponents' weak points, and he regularly proves he can do so in his battles with Goku and Vegeta.

A way to get Granolah and Frieza's recent new transformation, Black Frieza , into the anime, is that the two eventually duke it out. With Granolah's recent power-up wish, there isn't much time. The Cerealian gave up 150 years of his life to attain all the power levels he would've achieved in his life right away. The choice gives him a limited amount of time to find Frieza and defeat him.

Worlds are set to collide with Frieza's return in the arc and Granolah's hunt for him. In fact, at the time that the Frieza Force was around for the Cerealian destruction, King Cold and a non-canon Cooler would have been alive. This would be a great opportunity to bring the Frieza family back into the story and give them the proper, revenge-filled defeat at the hands of the last living Cerealian.

Granolah is canon, so it's not like bringing him into the fold would be that difficult. No retconning required, just an easy addition is all that needs to happen. Granolah would add another great fighter capable of going toe-to-toe with high-powered enemies and also a new ability that can aid the group. His long range attacks and quick-study of rival fighters could certainly come in handy. Should Granolah be brought into Dragon Ball Super 's anime future? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Cast Guide: All the Tributes, Mentors and Younger Versions of Characters in Prequel
articles.summary: Before Katniss Everdeen ever volunteered as tribute for the Hunger Games, another District 12 victor made his way out of the arena, but with much fewer odds in his favor. “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” is set 24 years before the first “Hunger Games” film (and 40 years after “The Ballad of Songbird […]
articles.content:
Joseph Zada stars as Haymitch Abernathy, a tribute from District 12 who is the future mentor to the main series’ protagonist, Katniss Everdeen. Despite being born on the same day as the Reaping, Haymitch’s birthday luck runs short when he is selected for the second Quarter Quell and soon finds himself on President Snow's radar after publicly defying the capitol.

Throughout the film, Haymitch is thrust into several intense moments, whether they are grounded in emotion or consist of demanding action sequences. One of Zada’s favorite scenes is a particular battle near the end of the film, which he tells Variety makes him “look like a fucking action star.”

“In terms of acting, I just want to throw myself completely in the deep end with every project. And it helps so much having that attitude in the arena, because that’s just my character the whole time,” Zada says. “He’s really going for it, and I was like, ‘There’s no way for me to do this believably unless I’m throwing myself down that mountain or pushing myself to the edge of death and almost injuring myself every single day. There was no other way for me to do that and make it believable without just completely diving in the deep end.”

Haymitch Abernathy was played by Woody Harrelson in the original films.

Joining Haymitch in the second Quarter Quell is District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner, who's played by Mckenna Grace and is the original owner of Katniss’ mockingjay pin. Initially at odds with her fellow District 12 tributes, Maysilee eventually joins their alliance with the Newcomers and grows particularly close to Haymitch, encouraging him to defy the Capitol.

As a long-time fan of the “Hunger Games” franchise, Grace tells Variety she wanted her portrayal of Maysilee to be accurate to Collins’ source material. One of the things she prioritized was keeping the character’s anger consistent throughout the film instead of having her arc of “learning to be kinder diminish her anger.

“While she finds happiness in being kind to the people around her and protecting them, she's still a very angry character. And I think that it's really important to show young women and anyone in general that the two can coexist,” she says. “You can be very angry at the world, or you can be very loud about the things that you believe in and in standing up for yourself and the people around you. But you can also be kind throughout that.

Grace also portrays Merilee Donner, Maysilee’s twin sister. Her previous credits include “I, Tonya,” “Regretting You,” “The Handmaid’s Tale” and “Ghostbusters: Afterlife.” She is next set to star in “Scooby Doo: Origins” as a young Daphne Blake.

Lenore Dove Baird is Haymitch’s girlfriend and a descendant of the Covey, which Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zelger) was a part of in "Songbirds and Snakes." After her mother died during childbirth, Lenore Dove was raised by her uncles Tam Amber and Clerk Carmine Clade, whom audiences met in the previous prequel. Whitney Peak plays the character after starring in films like “Molly’s Game” and series such as “Chilling Adventures of Sabrina.”

Ralph Fiennes stars as Coriolanus Snow, the cruel and tyrannical president of Panem who previously mentored Lucy Gray Baird, a District 12 tribute who won the 10th Hunger Games. After Haymitch publicly defies the Capitol, Snow marks him as a target and stops at nothing to suppress his resistance. No stranger to playing the villain, Fiennes has also starred as the antagonist in “The Menu” and as Voldemort in the “Harry Potter” franchise. Snow was played by Donald Sutherland in the original films and by Tom Blyth in “The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes.”

Elle Fanning plays Effie Trinket, a Capitol stylist who steps in to help dress the District 12 tributes for their interviews. Effie ultimately becomes the district’s escort in the original films, where she was played by Elizabeth Banks. Earlier this year, Fanning received an Emmy nomination for “Margo’s Got Money Troubles” after previously starring in “A Complete Unknown,” “Maleficent” and “Super 8.”

Plutarch Heavensbee is a cameraman assigned to cover District 12 during the Hunger Games. Although he serves as a trusted advisor to President Snow, Plutarch is secretly involved in the growing rebellion against the Capitol and helps Haymitch execute his plan to break the arena. He’s played by Jesse Plemons, who also starred in “Bugonia,” “The Power of the Dog,” “Kinds of Kindness” and “Game Night.” Plutarch ultimately becomes a gamemaker for the third Quarter Quell in “Catching Fire,” where he is played by Philip Seymour Hoffman for the remainder of the original films.

As the host of the Hunger Games, Caesar Flickerman is responsible for keeping Capitol citizens entertained and invested throughout the annual event. Typically known for his bold outfits and quick-witted humor, the role was originated by Stanley Tucci and is now played by Kieran Culkin, whose previous credits include “Succession” and “A Real Pain.” Caesar's grandfather Lucky (Jason Schwartzman) was the announcer in "Songbirds and Snakes."

Drusilla Sickle is a Capitol chaperone for the District 12 tributes. Openly disdainful of the poor district, particularly Maysilee, Drusilla hopes to earn a promotion to a higher-ranking group of tributes and takes extreme measures to ensure her presentations are nothing short of perfection. Glenn Close stars as the vain escort after playing a similarly eccentric character in “101 Dalmatians.” She is also known for her roles in “Fatal Attraction” and “Dangerous Liaisons.”

Billy Porter plays Magno Stift, a reptile-loving Capitol stylist unwillingly assigned to the District 12 tributes. Magno puts little effort into dressing the tributes on the rare occasion he decides to show up. Porter is largely known for his stage career, having starred in Broadway shows including “Kinky Boots,” “Cabaret” and “Shuffle Along.”

After winning the 34th Hunger Games, Beetee secretly conspired against the Capitol, which President Snow eventually discovered. Now, Snow is punishing the District 3 victor by reaping his son, Ampert, for the second Quarter Quell. Kelvin Harrison Jr. plays the character after starring in films including “Mufasa: The Lion King" and “Elvis." Jeffrey Wright originated the role in the previous films.

Also a fan of the franchise, Harrison Jr. tells Variety that, while he would refer to the books and Wright's performance, he primarily focused on the world and character that the screenwriters of "Sunrise on the Reaping" created for that specific moment in time.

"What they [the screenwriters] gave me the real estate for was really fleshing out a sense of knowingness that there is no space for grief for him right now. He is in a position where there isn't self-preservation," Harrison Jr. says. "There is overcoming in order to have a larger cause to take care of a larger party, and what's at stake is his own flesh and blood. And I wanted to figure out how to navigate the feeling of grief as something you can't really control, but you're trying to outrun it. But you really can't."

Harrison Jr. and Wright previously played father and son in 2018's "Monster" and will do so again in "Samo Lives," the upcoming Jean-Michel Basquiat biopic.

Wiress is the exceptionally intelligent victor of the 49th Hunger Games who, alongside Mags, mentors Haymitch, Maysilee, Wyatt and Lou Lou for the second Quarter Quell. She is played by Maya Hawke, who is known for her roles in “Stranger Things,” “Do Revenge” and “Inside Out 2,” and was originated by Amanda Plummer in “The Hunger Games: Catching Fire.”

Little is known about Wiress beyond the fact that her arena was filled with mirrors and that she won without killing a single tribute. Hawke tells Variety she "relished in" every piece of information she could find about the character, hoping to portray a version of Wiress who was "beautiful, curious, kind of shy and uniquely capable."

"I imagine that she probably lost some allies and some friends in her games, and that emotionally attaching to these young people now would be a living nightmare," Hawke says about Wiress' relationships with the District 12 tributes. "It's like I'm trying to see them as pigs, and could one of these pigs work for my protest? I'm trying not to see them as human, and what I tried to build in was that she slowly starts to see them as human, and that's how she gets so messed up."

Mags, the winner of the 11th Hunger Games from District 4, mentors the District 12 tributes for the 50th games. She is played by Lili Taylor, who also starred in “The Conjuring,” “Mystic Pizza” and “American Crime,” and was originated by Lynn Cohen in “The Hunger Games: Catching Fire.”

Taylor tells Variety she avoided relying too heavily on Cohen's performance, instead focusing on who Mags was at this particular point in her life rather than the character's eventual fate. Working with director Francis Lawrence, the two created a version of Mags that served as a motherly figure to her tributes.

“In some ways, Mags just really cares about those young mentees and will do whatever she can to help them, even under the circumstances,” she says. “It’s so strange when you really think about it deeply, but it’s sort of like they [the tributes] have a job to do, and I really like them, and I want them to do well.”

Jennifer Lawrence reprises her role as Katniss Everdeen, the protagonist of the original “Hunger Games” films. Reaped for the 74th games, the District 12 tribute became the face of the rebellion with her mockingjay pin, which was passed down from Maysilee Donner. Since joining the franchise in 2012, Lawrence has starred in films including “Silver Linings Playbook,” “Die My Love” and “No Hard Feelings.”

Peeta Mellark is Katniss’ fellow District 12 victor of the 74th Hunger Games and her love interest in the original films, making him a key role in the rebellion. Josh Hutcherson returns to the role 11 years after the release of “The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 2″ and has since starred in the “Five Nights at Freddy’s” films and “I Love LA.”

The role of Haymitch Abernathy was originated by Woody Harrelson in the original films, where he served as the heavy-drinking, hard-shelled mentor to Katniss and Peeta. Secretly conspiring with Capitol insiders, Haymitch helped launch the start of the rebellion and oversaw the dethroning of President Snow. Harrelson's additional credits include "Cheers," "Brothers" and "Now You See Me."

Proserpina Trinket is Effie’s younger sister and a Capitol prep team member assigned to Haymitch for the Quarter Quell. Played by Iris Apatow, the university student is constantly worrying her grade will be affected due to Magno’s failure to dress the District 12 tributes. Apatow’s previous credits include “Funny People,” “Knocked Up” and “This is 40.”

Working alongside Proserpina, Vitus is also a part of Haymitch’s Capitol prep team who is similarly apprehensive about how his grade will be affected. He is played by Edvin Ryding, who previously starred in “28 Years Later” and “Mother Goose.”

Ben Wang plays Wyatt Callow, the first male tribute from District 12 to be reaped. He and his family are widely known throughout the district as the “booker boys,” a name that reflects their illegal gambling business that takes bets on the annual Hunger Games. Wang plays the character after appearing in films like “The Long Walk,” “Karate Kid: Legends” and “Mean Girls.”

Molly McCann stars as Louella, Haymitch’s young neighbor in District 12 who is also selected to fight in the Quarter Quell. Often styled in two braids and having earned the nickname “sweetheart” by Haymitch, Louella offers many similarities to Katniss.

Iona Bell plays Lou Lou, a lookalike of Louella McCoy assigned by President Snow to serve as a District 12 tribute. Though her origins in the film are unknown, she was said to be from District 11 in Collins’ novel. This is Bell's first major film role.

Ampert is a District 3 tribute who is also the son of former victor Beetee Latier. He created the Newcomers alliance that would outnumber the Careers and helped Haymitch with his plans inside the arena. Ampert is played by Percy Daggs IV, who has also acted in “Never Let Go” and “Paradise.”

Silka is one of the female Careers — a tribute who’s trained to compete in the games from a young age — from District 1. Played by Laura Marcus, Silka is set on targeting Maysilee from their early interactions during training. Marcus’ credits also include “Death by Lightning” and “The Jetty.”

Panache is one of two male tributes from District 1 and a member of the Careers who personally targeted Haymitch since their first interaction, physically attacking him during training and vowing to kill him in the arena. He’s played by Jhaleil Swaby, who also appeared in “Neagley” earlier this year.

Rada Rae plays Wellie, one of the two female tributes from District 6. Though her role in the film is relatively limited, Wellie forms a trusting friendship with Haymitch in the novel, with the protagonist vowing to protect her as much as he could in the arena. Rae previously starred in Netflix’s “Exterritorial.”

Ringina is a District 7 tribute who is a part of the Newcomers alliance. She is played by Tatyana Muzondo, who is making her film debut.

Salimou Thiam plays District 9 tribute Clayton, who joins the Newcomers alongside Haymitch and Ampert.

Smylie Bradwell stars as Haymitch’s younger brother, Sid, who is two years short of having his name entered in the annual reaping. Largely introduced to audiences via “Hamnet,” Bradwell has also starred in “Faith” and “The Crow Girl.”

Burdock is the future father of Katniss Everdeen and Haymitch’s best friend in District 12. Played by Scot Greenan, Burdock first began dating Asterid around the second Quarter Quell and is also Lenore Dove’s distant relative. Phillip Troy Linger played the character in the original films.

Asterid is the future mother of Katniss who first began dating Burdock during the events of the second Quarter Quell. She is also a close friend of the Donner twins, standing with them at the reaping and sharing an emotional goodbye after Maysilee’s name was called.

articles.title: I’ve Been Waiting For A Home Town Season 11 Update, And Erin Napier Just Cleared Up The Confusion
articles.summary: It's all happening!
articles.content:
For the last decade, Ben and Erin Napier have been renovating homes in the small Southern town of Laurel, Mississippi, on HGTV’s wildly popular show Home Town . The series’ 10 th season premiered in January on the 2026 TV schedule , and fans, including me, have been itching for any sort of update on the famous reality couple. In particular, I’ve been waiting for an update on Season 11 , and Erin finally spoke out.

Considering it’s been a trying year for the Napiers , it’s great to see them finally able to celebrate something. Last December, the hotel they were renovating for their series, Home Town: Inn This Together , caught on fire, close to Erin’s 40 th birthday.

Welp, I didn't see this confusion coming. I’m excited to see what kind of houses the Napiers are renovating in the new season, which is billed as Season 10, but is actually Season 11. The Season 10 finale aired in March, so these new batch of episodes, coming sometime in 2027, will certainly be Season 11.

It’s definitely confusing, but I'm glad it was addressed. There are plenty of shows whose production numbers don’t line up with episode numbers, for whatever reason. For instance, a big Jeopardy! inconsistency Ken Jennings revealed last year was that the production numbers currently being used don’t equal the total number of episodes produced, all because of mistakes from decades ago.

articles.title: "I'm in Preparation for the End of Our World": Golshifteh Farahani on Art, War and Her Tallinn Premiere
articles.summary: After a thriller set as Kabul braces for the Taliban, the actress says her mind is on the state of the world and not on her next role.
articles.content:
Golshifteh Farahani ( Alpha , Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales ) is Leila, a young widow seeking a fresh start in Kabul, Afghanistan, in writer-director Chabname Zariab’s debut feature When She Hears the Bells (Les Clochettes de Kaboul) .

The France-based Iranian actress is attending the 30th edition of Estonia's Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ), where the film had its world premiere on Wednesday night in the First Feature Competition . After all, Leila soon finds out that the kitchen she works in is a so-called bacha bazi house. These are establishments in which boys and young men are forced to dress in women’s clothes and dance for entertainment — regularly followed by sexual exploitation. Set in 2021, the film also sees the Taliban moving ever closer to Kabul. Leila tries to flee while helping a group of boys escape before the city falls. Sayed Hashimi ( 13 Days, 13 Nights ) co-stars in the thriller, which includes images actually shot in Afghanistan. Le Pacte is handling sales.

Farahani talked to THR in Tallinn about When She Hears the Bells , why the film can speak to the Western world and why she isn't spending time thinking about her next project.

How did you find out about this film and decide to star in it?

Chabname wanted me for some time, but I wasn't reading the script because I was thinking I'd done The Patience Stone [set in war-torn Afghanistan]. So, it's a space for other actresses to do that. But she insisted and insisted and insisted, and at the end she said, "We're not going to do the movie [without you]." So, I ended up accepting the part without reading the script. I called her and said, "Let's do it." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I couldn't believe that this was Chabname's first feature script and her directorial debut.

When I read the script, I was also really surprised. It was amazing. The script is as good as the movie.

When She Hears the Bells combines thriller elements with the humane and emotional elements. How hard is that combination for you as the star?

I'm happy that I could see that it works because I'm very objective when I watch my movies. I know when it's bad and it doesn't work, and I know when it's good. Last night [during the premiere], I could feel this works because I constantly had goosebumps over goosebumps over goosebumps. I felt, "Yeah, the emotion works." For one of my friends, it is impossible to watch a movie without checking his phone. It was the first time I watched him not touching his phone, and at one point he just [leaned] forward. He was really engaged, and that was the best sign. The movie works. It really works.

There are all sorts of dark issues and threats in When She Hears the Bells . There is the bacha bazi, the situation of women, the encroaching Taliban. Do you see these as sharing any common themes?

The way I always look at it is that you're telling a story. It's just that the story is about horrible things. I think about the character who is actually in that situation, which is terrible. From the outside, when you watch it, it is unbearable. But the character is in it, so, as the character, I don't judge it as horrible. It's just that I'm living in that horror. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

As an audience, you say, "This is awful, this is horrible!" But as a character inside, you cannot say this is horrible. You just act on it.

Do you have any hopes for what audiences will take away from the film?

If the audience is moved by it and asks questions, if the movie is seen and appreciated, it's enough because so many of these movies can be so boring and so much.

These subjects are too much for the white man to even comprehend. Because sometimes the horror is too much for the civilized world. They can't even handle it. So they zap [it out] subconsciously.

But I think this movie works because it doesn't show the actual horror. If you saw the horror [committed against] a little boy in the film, the audience would zap. But because it's all left to the imagination, it keeps the white audience on a fine line of sitting and watching and feeling it, not blocking out the feeling.

This is the third year in a row that you have a film here at Tallinn. How much do you like the city and the festival? I love Tallinn, and I think the festival is great. I think people come here to watch movies, and the fact that this festival exists is a blessing because we all know the situation of the world and the budgets, and there are always challenges for these little festivals. But I come back to Tallinn anytime they ask me because I think it's a great festival. I have had three movies here: Reading Lolita in Tehran , Oh, What Happy Days! , and this one.

I'm a bit pessimistic, and I feel there's a big war coming. So, in my head, I feel we just need to prepare for a war. My headspace is not much in the artistic world, because I feel the situation of the world is so bad, and I feel that humanity needs to be prepared for war. Especially in Europe, people have been so spoiled, and I think the first place that is going to be completely smashed is Europe. So, in my headspace, I'm in preparation for the end of the world, the end of our world. I think we're going to enter a new order.

Who would start the war, or where? I just feel the world is going to go upside down. The world has become a minefield. No matter where you go, something is going to explode everywhere — every region you think of: America, Los Angeles, Florida, Africa, Europe, China, Taiwan. Everywhere you go, you might step on a mine, and it might explode. You just need to prepare.

articles.title: GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Actors Break Silence to Celebrate Release
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Rockstar Games Out of all the secrets Rockstar Games kept close to its chest regarding Grand Theft Auto 6, the identities of its two main actors were among the most closely guarded mysteries. Now that the game is finally out, the two actors behind Jason and Lucia have taken off their metaphorical balaclavas and spoken to the […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Out of all the secrets Rockstar Games kept close to its chest regarding Grand Theft Auto 6 , the identities of its two main actors were among the most closely guarded mysteries. Now that the game is finally out, the two actors behind Jason and Lucia have taken off their metaphorical balaclavas and spoken to the public.

Dylan Rourke and Manni L. Perez — Jason and Lucia, respectively — put out a joint Instagram post confirming their involvement with the critically acclaimed open-world game.

"Years witnessing the hardest working and most skilled artisans game making has to offer," reads the post. "We are truly honored to collaborate on this worldwide testament to human creativity, ingenuity, and sheer willpower. So much learned and so much to learn, keep fighting for what you love, stay humble. See y'all in Leonida."

View this post on Instagram While Rourke has been acting since 2013, this is his first video game role. Perez also started professionally acting the same year, but this is her second video game role; she was also "Clubber 2" and "Blackjack Dealer" in Grand Theft Auto 5 , making for one massive promotion. Neither of them post online very often, so their digital footprints are limited and don't contain many hints. As comical musician "Weird" Al Yankovic confirmed , there were non-disclosure agreements attached to the project, meaning those involved broadly couldn't confirm their roles. Their follower counts have grown considerably, though, as Perez now has about 434,000 followers on Instagram, while Rourke has around 122,000.

Lucia's actor was confirmed just prior to this Instagram announcement in a strange way. The nominees for the 2026 Game Awards came out on November 17th , which had Perez up for best performance in GTA 6 . It didn't say who she was playing, although, despite official confirmation, it was pretty obvious. Some also saw this as peculiar because it was one day before review embargoes lifted and two days before launch. However, it was clear judges who were playing GTA 6 during the secretive review period gave her the nod .

But some have been on this trail for years now. Most recently, Perez hosted a livestream in October where she was avoiding comments about GTA 6 . Various internet sleuths in 2024 also noted how Rourke and Perez were likely the two leads, which came after a lot of cross-referencing and social media-powered investigations. Others had an inkling the year prior, pointing to various similarities between Perez and Lucia. The corkboard full of red string had some failed leads, but some were entirely on the money, despite how tenuous the connections seemed at the time.

What do you think of Manni's and Dylan's performances? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: I'm Loving Netflix's Win The Mall (And Haley Baylee), But There's One Thing I'd Like To See More Of
articles.summary: I can't be the only one who's ever wondered what it would be like to spend a night in the mall.
articles.content:
Spoiler alert! This story discusses the ultimate winners of the reality competition series Win the Mall, now available with a Netflix subscription .

When you move 10 teams of two contestants into a shopping mall to compete for a $1 million grand prize, it feels like you should have a plan to incorporate the mall as much as possible. Part shopping spree and part social strategy, players are dropped into a real mall, but the fake storefronts make it challenging to fully utilize the mall itself, leaving it all to feel a bit disconnected at times.

Surprisingly, one of the highlights of Win the Mall is TikTok creator-turned- host Haley Baylee , who is truly delightful. She’s a likable host who can wear anything and look like she’s on a runway, but she also never takes herself too seriously, being goofy when she needs to be and taking on a more serious persona while tempting contestants with possible game advantages.

EXCLUSIVE : Edward Burns' micro-budget black-and-white family drama Beneath the Blue Suburban Skies debuted at the Toronto Film Festival in 2019.

Seven years later, the film is finally getting a release with a one-week awards-qualifying theatrical run in New York from December 25, ahead of a rollout in major cities in January.

The film stars Burns alongside Tony and BAFTA winner Jennifer Ehle with Hannah Dunne and Brian Wiles also among cast. Multi-hyphenate Burns is getting behind the film's release via his production company Marlboro Road Gang Productions. There aren't many notices for the film online. The few that can be found are positive. Variety's review of the movie from 2019 praised the performances and Ehle in particular.

Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault last Monday. articles.title: 'American Doctor' Director on Her Powerful Gaza Doc: "I Wanted to Do Something"
articles.summary: Poh Si Teng spent 22 years as a journalist and documentary facilitator before a calling to chronicle life and death in Gaza hospitals led to her directorial debut.
articles.content:
"I know the film is called American Doctor , but it's not actually about the American doctors," Poh Si Teng told The Hollywood Reporter at the recent SCAD Savannah Film Festival , referencing the three American physicians — one Jewish, one Palestinian and one Zoroastrian — who are documented in her film as they volunteer at hospitals in Gaza amid the ongoing war there. "It's about their relationships with the Palestinian doctors. This is how we bring it back to the United States."

American Doctor , which premiered at Sundance in January and was released by Watermelon Pictures in August, was a selection of the SCAD Savannah Film Fest’s celebrated Docs to Watch sidebar. As a result, Teng participated in a Q&A following a screening of it for a capacity crowd at the SCAD Museum of Art — which you can watch above — and was also one of 10 directors of outstanding 2026 docs who appeared on the fest’s Doc to Watch Panel . Related Stories Movies Ron Howard Wasn't Sure He Was the Right Director for 'Avedon'; This Is What Changed His Mind SCAD Savannah Film Festival 'Cookie Queens' Director Says Girl Scout Cookies Were "A Delicious Way In" to a Larger Conversation (Video)

Born in Malaysia but now based in the United States, she had never directed a feature film prior to American Doctor . She had worked as a cameraperson for AP, a reporter for the New York Times , a documentary commissioner for Al Jazeera, a studio executive for ABC and a grants director for the International Documentary Association. But then she felt a calling. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"For a long time, I guess for 22 years of my life, I just never felt that my voice as a director was needed," she explained. "I thought it would be a better use of my time and my skills to support other directors. But when the genocide happened, and seeing colleagues of mine at Al Jazeera being targeted and executed, I wanted to do something. I thought maybe it was time."

Sporting a shirt proclaiming "HOSPITALS SHOULD NOT BE TARGETED," she recounted her first impressions of the three American doctors: "When I met them I thought, 'You couldn't be more different. How do you work with each other? How is it possible?'" These were among the questions that led her to try to raise funds to make a documentary. But she quickly found that few institutions were willing to financially support a documentary about the current turmoil in the Middle East.

So she emptied her savings account of $150,000, rallied additional support from a wide range of artists, musicians and activists, and assembled a team of people hailing from eight different countries to film over 50 days spread between the Christmases of 2024 and 2025. She herself could not enter Gaza, so she recruited local filmmakers, who were suffering under the strain of the Israeli blockade of their city, to capture life and death in and around area hospitals.

The film opens with the Jewish-American doctor, Dr. Mark Perlmutter, chastising Teng for her hesitancy to include in the film a photograph of children killed by an Israeli airstrike. She recalled, "Mark set the tone for what the film was going to be, and there was no turning back after that." Still, it was important to Teng that the film be narratively engaging, so she found structural "points of inspiration" from sources like The Pitt , Chernobyl and The Babadook .

Her conclusion: "If you see 'the other' as your own — if we saw Palestinians as we would see ourselves — we would be more willing to fight for them, especially when it has everything to do with our taxpayer money being used to harm them."

articles.title: Judge Weighs Whether To Allow Kennedy Center To Proceed With Closure Plan
articles.summary: A federal judge said that he will issue a ruling "as soon as I can" as to whether the Kennedy Center can proceed with its plan to close the arts complex for two years for renovations, amid fears that President Donald Trump ultimately will move to demolish the 55-year-old arts complex. articles.content:
A federal judge said that he will issue a ruling "as soon as I can" as to whether the Kennedy Center can proceed with its plan to close the arts complex for two years for renovations, amid fears that President Donald Trump ultimately will move to demolish the 55-year-old arts complex.

U.S. District Court Judge Christopher Cooper issued an injunction earlier this year that barred the center from closing unless its board conducted a more thorough analysis of its impacts on programming and other operations. The judge also ordered that Trump's name be removed from the complex, with a tarp now covering the front facade after crews removed the lettering to comply with the order. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Legal Grand Trump Accomplishment: POTUS Defeats NYT Move To Toss $15B 'Lucky Loser' Defamation Suit News CBS And Paramount+ To Air Next Kennedy Center Honors

The Justice Department, representing the center, is seeking to lift the injunction, arguing that the board vote in August and September to close the center sufficiently examined all of the options, citing a report from Delta Consulting Group. The report concluded that a two-year closure would be much less expensive than keeping the center open during construction, a process that would take four years. "The court contemplated the exact course of action the center took here," William Jankowski, attorney for the DOJ, told the judge.

An attorney for Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-OH), an ex officio board member of the center who is challenging the board's actions, argued that, despite the third-party Delta analysis, the board still has not considered the impact of a closure on such things as fundraising and programming.

Nathaniel Zelinsky, Beatty's attorney, said that the board "keeps rubber stamping the same decision." Trump, who is the board chairman, announced the closure plan in February, but Beatty's legal team has claimed that the decision was not motivated by the renovation, but to mask the embarrassment of a drop in revenue after Trump's name was added to the center's official moniker.

Zelinsky also pointed to another analysis conducted by real estate firm, which showed that a four-year renovation plan that kept the center open would be far less costly than the Delta analysis. The center itself has had scant major programming since July, and the sprawling main building has been off limits to the public since September. The center says that the closure is temporary due to safety concerns, after a portion of the indoor ceiling plaster collapsed following rainstorms, as well as concerns of deterioration of supports for exterior soffit panels.

Meanwhile, the center is going ahead with its annual Kennedy Center Honors, but in an alternate venue: The Capitol One Arena. The event is scheduled to take place on Dec. 7 and air on CBS on Dec. 27. The center also plans to proceed with the Mark Twain Prize, an annual ceremony honoring comedians and humorists, next year, Jankowski told the judge.

Trump has stirred concerns over demolition of the center after he raised the prospect in social media posts. He also was photographed on Air Force One in September reviewing a poster board that featured the lettering, "Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED."

While the DOJ attorney argued that Trump's remarks are not relevant to whether to lift the injunction, the judge still expressed concerns. In September, he ordered that he be given at least a 30-day notice before any such drastic changes be made to the center.

Norm Eisen , who also is representing Beatty, told reporters that they were trying to prevent a scenario like what happened to the White House East Wing, which Trump ordered demolished last year to make room for a new ballroom, and the East Potomac Golf Course, where the National Park Service abruptly cut down hundreds of trees on a site that the president wants to remake into championship links.

"The most important takeaway: There is no question in my mind that this judge, under any cirumstances, is going to allow the demolition of the Kennedy Center, just that East Wing or East Potomac Golf Course wrecking ball scenario," Eisen said.

articles.title: Spider-Man’s Darkest Storyline Just Made His Most Iconic Power Deadlier than Ever
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Spider-Man has a whole host of iconic powers, from sticking to walls to backflipping like nobody else, but there's no debate that his most unique and interesting power is definitely his Spider-Sense. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Spider-Man has a whole host of iconic powers, from sticking to walls to backflipping like nobody else, but there's no debate that his most unique and interesting power is definitely his Spider-Sense. This preternatural ability lets Peter detect any danger before it reaches him or those around him, and that both keeps him safe and gives him an unmatched edge when he gets into a fight. It's a power that's so ingrained in everything Spider-Man does that it almost becomes invisible, but is always felt. It also has one of the most iconic signifiers in all of comics, immediately telling the audience everything they need to know.

However, even this spectacular power is completely different in the Midnight Universe. This dark new reality has completely reimagined Marvel's most iconic characters. For Spider-Man , that means that his great power now comes with great monstrosity, as the spider that bit him turned him into a creature that is no longer human . This has affected every part of his character, but the biggest shift we saw in Midnight Spider-Man #2 is that his Spider-Sense doesn't just warn him about danger, but takes him over to actively dispatch it.

Given that he transformed into a horrible monster from the spider fusing onto his chest, Peter didn't bring his signed Oscorp contract to Felicia, which landed her in some hot water. She took two of Oscorp's bruisers to his house to find him, but realized how horrible things were when Gargan happened upon what was left of Uncle Ben. Then Peter crawled down from the wall and begged Felicia for help. The goons tried to blast him, but Peter's new instincts kicked in and he went on the offensive. His Spider-Sense forced him to attack , and he did it with relentless abandon, literally ripping the two men apart before diving out the window.

This Peter obviously has no experience in combat. He's probably never even been in a fight before, but here he rushed forward and killed two people without hesitation. Importantly, he didn't attack Felicia, as he didn't register her as a threat. This new Spider-Sense carries a much, much stronger response, tapping into his fight response instead of his flight. This Peter rushes into danger instead of pulling away from it, and it can even override his mind. We know that Peter was hardly aware of what happened because he was practically a walking zombie after he escaped. This is a total rework of how his Spider-Sense works, bringing it closer to the monstrous ideal of this universe.

Before he even officially became Spider-Man, Peter had already killed two people, which his mainline counterpart would never do. The two guards in question weren't just throwaways, either, as they were called Gargan and Rodriquez. Those happen to be the names of Scorpion and Tarantula, and given that one had his face removed and the other parted ways with the vast majority of his organs, it's safe to say that they are dead. This comic has gone out of its way to show that nobody is safe in this new reality, and with a literal beastly side that can take over Peter and kill whoever it deems a threat, it's clear that these are far from the last bodies Peter will put in the ground .

Still, this doesn't mean that this is the last we'll see of these two. It's entirely possible that Doc Ock will use his horrific science to resurrect them, as they've come into contact with Peter and could have been changed in some capacity. Either way, Peter has a long, hard war ahead of him, and none of his nightmare villains are going to be willing to walk away with a few lumps on their heads. They will be corporate monsters created for the sole purpose of capturing or killing him, and no law will stop them.

A huge part of this storyline is definitely going to be Peter drawing a line between what he considers his monstrous new reality and the humanity he can't afford to lose. He'll be forced to either come to terms with killing or force himself to constantly be in control. Either way, he'll have to confront the monster that lives inside of him, both literally and metaphorically. Aunt May, who seems to have left Uncle Ben in this world, could prove to be his last connection to humanity and pull him out of the abyss. Spider-Man is going to have to become something more, or else he'll just be another monster.

What do you think of this change in how Peter's Spider-Sense works? Let us know in the comments below!

The actor, who was 86 at the time of his passing, died on Wednesday, October 28th in Los Angeles after what was described as a “brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia.” Now, the beloved actor’s death certificate has been issue and confirms the conditions as well as offers additional details.

According to TMZ, Stewart died from Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia as had previously been reported. The certificate specifically details cardiopulmonary arrest and a neurocognitive disorder with Lewy body — Lewy body dementia, which is a progressive form of dementia that affects not just memory and thinking but movement as well. Other details of the official death certificate also include that Stewart’s remains underwent a process called alkaline hydrolysis, more commonly known as water cremation. It’s a form of cremation that uses water and chemicals rather than high heat and flames.

articles.summary: 'Love Is Blind' is the top original show, but the bar is lower than it's been in more than two years.
articles.content:
Netflix's Love Is Blind led the original series chart in Nielsen's streaming ratings for the week of Nov. 2-8. But that's not saying a whole lot — it was a very soft week for original streaming shows.

On the acquired series chart, however, From put up more big numbers. The sci-fi/horror series led the overall rankings for a third straight week .

Love Is Blind' s 691 million minutes of viewing time were enough to lead the original series top 10, but that total is the lowest for the top original show in more than two years. The last time the No. 1 original was lower was in early August 2024, when The Boys had 662 million viewing minutes. articles.title: Steven Spielberg Gently Pitched Christopher Nolan The Movie Idea I Think Fans Have Been Wanting
articles.summary: This follow-up makes all too much sense.
articles.content:
I don't know how you follow a $1.8 billion trip through Greek mythology , but Steven Spielberg apparently has an idea. Christopher Nolan is still taking a victory lap for The Odyssey , one of the biggest hits on the 2026 movie schedule , and the Jaws director just floated a follow-up I'd pay good money to see. The way he brought it up made me laugh, too. Even Hollywood legends know how to suggest another movie without sounding too pushy.

I love how politely Spielberg slid that into the conversation. It's the cinematic equivalent of complimenting somebody's enormous Thanksgiving dinner and then asking what they're making next year. He even followed it up by insisting there was no pressure. Nolan, understandably, joked that Spielberg seemed to be speaking for Universal Pictures. Spielberg admitted the studio would probably appreciate it, but he was interested himself.

Nolan has already explained why he chose The Odyssey . He considers The Iliad more grounded, while the later poem's monsters and stranger adventures offered something he hadn't seen done the way he envisioned. That doesn't mean he couldn't change his mind, especially after his latest movie has reportedly earned more than $1.8 billion worldwide.

articles.title: GTA 6 Removes "Iconic" Prostitutes Feature, and Fans Are Angry
articles.summary: Unlike in previous Grand Theft Auto games, players can't hire prostitutes in GTA 6, and this has proven to be one of the biggest talking points of launch week, at least on social media. This is the first Grand Theft Auto game in the 3D era, starting in 2001 with GTA III, which introduced prostitutes […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Unlike in previous Grand Theft Auto games, players can't hire prostitutes in GTA 6 , and this has proven to be one of the biggest talking points of launch week, at least on social media. This is the first Grand Theft Auto game in the 3D era, starting in 2001 with GTA III , which introduced prostitutes to the series. Since then, they have been in GTA: Vice City, GTA San Andreas , GTA 4 , and GTA 5 . Going into the release of Grand Theft Auto VI , there was no word of this content being removed, making it a surprise for fans of the series. And it's not a surprise many like.

While many Grand Theft Auto players, if not the majority, are not very bothered by the change from Rockstar Games, there are plenty who. To this end, many of the top posts right now on the GTA 6 Unmoderated Reddit page are about this topic, including the very top post.

Not only are Grand Theft Auto fans unhappy that the feature has been removed, but they also claim it's emblematic of the rest of the game, which limits player freedom compared to previous installments, especially when it comes to romance.

"Removing prostitutes from the game makes no sense at all," reads the title of one of the top posts on the aforementioned Reddit page over the last 24 hours. The post continues, "It’s been an iconic feature in the franchise for a long time, but they suddenly decide to scrap it because Jason has to stay loyal to Lucia. Did we just forget that Michael was able to pick up hookers and cheat on his wife in GTA 5 ? It’s supposed to be an unhinged game where anything can happen.

There are many of these posts not just on Reddit, but across the Internet. It's indeed odd that Rockstar Games allows players not to romance Jason and Lucia, yet doesn't let them have other romantic opportunities. You're either locked into the romance or locked into nothing. Rockstar Games has its official explanation , but its official explanation doesn't actually explain a lot. It effectively boils down to not undermining and harming the Bonnie-and-Clyde-esque story that is central to the game, but in the process, it undermines and harms other elements of the series.

This ties into a larger problem with the game, which is that the realism and immersion it puts on a pedestal is often fundamentally at odds with the over-the-top and zany DNA of the series. It worked in Red Dead Redemption 2 because Red Dead Redemption is more grounded, slow-moving, and not as chaotic. To this end, GTA 6 feels far more like RDR2 than any other previous GTA game in many ways.

All of that said, and as always, feel free to leave a comment or two letting us know what you think. Was this the right call by Rockstar Games?

articles.content:
Hollywood has spent a good many years trying to adapt British cult classic TV series The Prisoner into a feature film.

Now, however, a producer and a streamer are taking a ride on the penny-farthing back to the original medium.

Amazon Studios has picked up the rights to The Prisoner for a modern take on the series. Angry Films’ Susan Montford and Don Murphy , lifelong fans of the 1967 series who secured the rights, will executive produce, as will Philippe Maigret and Lucianne Papon of ITV, the company which originally distributed the show. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Mariko Tamaki Writing Sexy Vampire Thriller 'Royal Blood' for Skybound, Image Comics (Exclusive) Lifestyle T-Mobile Introduces T-Mix, an Innovative Phone Plan That Lets You Choose What's Included

The new potential series is a priority for the streamer which is already out to showrunners. The new story will be set in modern times.

The original series was a blend of sci-fi, spy craft, and psychological drama set against the paranoia and existential angst of the Cold War at the time. Patrick McGoohan starred as an intelligence agent who is kidnapped and awakens in a remote town known as the Village. Like all the residents, his name is stripped from him and he becomes known only as Number Six. McGoohan spends the series squaring off against Number Two and Number One, not knowing whom he can trust in the town as he tries to escape.

The show only lasted one season but its reach was long, thanks in part to some avant-garde, swinging sixties production values and an ending that left the audience hanging. It has been cited as an influence on shows such as Twin Peaks, X-Files and Lost . And it has mesmerized filmmakers such as Christopher Nolan, who mulled a movie adaptation. articles.summary: Rossi Gifford is drawing the ongoing series that will debut early next year.
articles.content:
Mariko Tamaki grew up reading the vampire stories by author Anne Rice and became enthralled by the mix of horror and brooding romance.

“I've always loved a heartfelt monster story, and to me she is the queen of the soulful vampire,” the award-winning graphic novel author and creator said via email to The Hollywood Reporter .

Now Tamaki, who has spent the last several years working on DC’s YA graphic novels and is known for her queer coming-of-age story Laura Dean Keeps Breaking Up with Me , will channel some of that love into her own romantic vampire comic book series. She is set to write Royal Blood , an ongoing original horror series from Skybound and Image Comics. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Sam Reid Plays Bloodsucking Rock Star in 'The Vampire Lestat' Trailer From AMC TV AMC Cancels 'Talamasca: The Secret Order' After One Season

Tamaki is working with artist Rossi Gifford ( Batman: Bad Seeds – Streets of Gotham ) on the series, with the duo acting as co-creators along with Glenn Geller, Skybound’s president of TV.

Colorist Miquel Muerto (an apt name for someone who also works on Something is Killing the Children ) and letterer Becca Carey ( Exquisite Corpses ) are on also part of the creative team for the comic, which is due to arrive in shops and digital platforms on Feb. 24, 2027. The book is intended for mature readers.

Hearts will skip, and many will stop entirely, in this story that Geller described as “Shakespeare with fangs.” Royal Blood is centered on a prince named Oliver, who is struggling to understand his place in the royal family, and a vampire, Charlotte, who was sent to destroy the royal family. Tamaki called it as “a sexy spy story, a vampire story, and an impossible love story.” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The initial idea of the series came from Skybound’s Geller, who posited, “What if a vampire spy infiltrated the royal family by seducing the prince?” Geller came up with the concept, title and main character names and showed it to his Skybound colleagues. Skybound Editorial loved the idea and wanted to make it a comic, reaching out to Tamaki, whom they thought would be a perfect fit given her track record.

Tamaki has gained a strong reader following thanks to a body of work that focuses on relationships, identity, and coming-of-age stories, LGBT or otherwise. Her graphic novel Laura Dean won the 2019 Harvey Award for best children or young adult book and was nominated for the Harvey for book of the year. It won three Ignatz Awards and three Eisners, including one for best writer and best publication for teens. More recently she wrote DC’s YA graphic novel I Am Not Starfire as well as the mini-series Zatanna: Bring Down the House .

For Royal Blood , Tamaki pitched a more fleshed out version of the idea and wrote a few scripts. Gifford was then brought in as artist, adding to what became the final form of the series. All three are working together on the ongoing series.

Tamaki listened to Annie Lennox's "Love Song for a Vampire” plenty while writing the comic. The song appeared Bram Stoker’s Dracula , Francis Ford Coppola’s adaptation of perhaps the most famous vampire story of all time. It’s a movie she loves and notes the costumes by Eiko Ishioka as a standout. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Like the Rice novels and the Coppola movie, this comic is intended to have an undercurrent of passion running through it.

“It is so sexy, I can't even tell you,” said Tamaki. “It is sooo sexy. I wrote it a little sexy and then Rossi Gifford made it sooo sexy.”

Gifford is a Toronto-based artist and character-designer who is coming off of working on DC’s Batman: Bad Seeds – Streets of Gotham . Tamaki and Skybound found a smoldering aspect to her work that made her the choice to draw the series.

“With Mariko’s work, which I’ve followed for years, at its heart, we have all the ingredients for a compelling series: engaging characters, a thrilling plot, horror, drama and a spicy love story,” said Gifford in a statement.

Royal Blood will be the latest title in Skybound’s line of horror comics that famously began with The Walking Dead . This year it published Corpse Knight , written by The Conjuring franchise director Michael Chaves, and continues to put out re-imaginings of iconic horror properties with the licenses of Creepshow and the Universal Monsters line.

articles.title: Guardians of the Galaxy Almost Had a Very Different Baby Groot, and You Can Now Own the Strange Original Design
articles.summary: The Walt Disney Company Before there was Baby Yoda, there was another movie character capturing the hearts of moviegoers back in 2017. While the character made his debut as a huge, old walking talking tree - with a very limited vocabulary - after a self-sacrificing moment in Guardians of the Galaxy, he returned as a small sapling ready to […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Before there was Baby Yoda, there was another movie character capturing the hearts of moviegoers back in 2017. While the character made his debut as a huge, old walking talking tree - with a very limited vocabulary - after a self-sacrificing moment in Guardians of the Galaxy , he returned as a small sapling ready to grow again over the course of several movies. That character is Groot, a part of the Marvel superhero team whose importance is often overlooked for his comical iterations of "I am Groot" in response to everything, who became Baby Groot at the end of the first movie and appeared in said form throughout the second adventure for Star Lord, Gamora, Drax, Rocket and their ever-changing and expanding group. But a new auction is giving fans the chance to own an original design for the character by effects master Phil Tippett and it is very different to the one we thankfully got.

Being sold by Heritage Auctions , this lot features a sculpted maquette of Groot's second form following his "death" in Guardians of the Galaxy . Instead of the cute and strangely cuddly plant-like being, Tippett's proposed design is captured in this piece is a grotesque "old man" Groot with almost pained expression and long spindly limbs. Although the character does have a Groot feel about it, it has a haunted quality that really would not have allowed retailers to stock up on cute cuddly toys and merchandise with its face on. The maquette is made of Magic Sculpt clay, painted in brown to make it look like it is made of wood. The piece is finished off by coming with its own terracotta plant pot with clay "soil" to make it looks like it is actually rooted into the container. The piece is certainly something that could be a talking point as part of any collection, and at the moment it is selling for what seems like a steal at $1,000. Whether it remains at that level is yet to be seen, but if so, then someone will get a great deal.

While Groot is usually involved in the comical side of the MCU, he is a character that has been involved in some of the most pivotal moments the Guardians have faced . In their first outing in 2014, Groot protects the team from being killed in the final act, enclosing the group in his branches and ultimately sacrificing himself for their survival. At the same time, this act prevented the Power Stone from falling into the hands of Ronan, which could have had consequences long before Thanos was able to finally acquire it before Infinity War . The result of Groot's sacrifice was a small shoot of his own being, which then would grow into Baby Groot by the second movie. Again, this form of Groot became the savior of the day, as his size allowed him to carry explosives to the core of Ego the living planet and destroy the megalomaniacal celestial being.

In Infinity War, a now teenage Groot was once again key in several moments, most prominently during the making of Thor's newly forged Stormbreaker by pulling together the pieces of the weapon and cutting off his own arm to create a handle for the weapon. Without the new ax, Thor would not have been able regain his powers and join the Avengers, even if their battle this time around ended in defeat to Thanos. Although it has not been revealed when the Guardians will return after their third solo outing, their future could depend on the events of Secret Wars . James Gunn previously worked on all Guardians stories and with his tenure as DC Studios CEO now over there is a chance he could return for a fourth movie, but there is just as much a chance that Marvel Studios will take the opportunity to prune the main Guardians group form the roster in Phase 7.

Would the original design of Baby Groot have ruined the character? Should the Guardians return to the MCU? Let us know in the comments.

The celebration, held at the historic event venue Storied in Chelsea, drew its own share of distinguished guests. While late-night host Jimmy Fallon was among the A-listers at NBC, his Tonight Show drummer, Roots frontman Ahmir “Questlove” Thompson, made a surprise appearance at the FSG gathering, delivering a DJ set.
